findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, so the MySQL endpoint is assigned a public IP and can be reached from the internet (combined with the wide ingress rule on the DB security group).
storage_encrypted = false leaves the catalog database's storage and snapshots unencrypted, exposing all stored data if the underlying volumes or backups are accessed.

The DB password (var.password) and DB username are interpolated into the EC2 user_data script and written to /tmp/dbinfo.inc and /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc, so the database credential is stored in plaintext on the instance, in the launch template/user-data record, and potentially world-readable on disk.
The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*", giving the application server full control of storage, compute, and databases including the ability to delete or exfiltrate all data.
MySQL port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR, so every host in the VPC (not just the app server's security group) can reach the database.
The database security group allows all outbound traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 on all protocols and ports, enabling data exfiltration or outbound C2 from a compromised DB host.
The master username is the well-known default "admin", which simplifies credential-guessing and credential-stuffing attacks against the publicly accessible database.

The deployed PHP builds SQL by string interpolation in the AddEmployee/VerifyEmployeesTable paths and reflects POST input (NAME, ADDRESS) without server-side validation, so the application is vulnerable to SQL injection even though mysqli_real_escape_string is applied inconsistently.

The AMI is selected with most_recent = true and a wildcard name filter, so instances may be launched from an unintended or compromised image if a matching image appears; the filter is not pinned to a specific, verified AMI ID.
skip_final_snapshot = true means the database can be destroyed without a final backup, and no deletion protection is enabled, risking unrecoverable data loss on accidental or malicious deletion.

character_set_client and character_set_server are set to utf8 (which is not the restrictive utf8mb4 and historically permits multi-byte bypass issues) applied immediately, which can weaken input handling for the attached database.
